title: Midquarter signal sprint - manager prep & self-coaching (Riley Morgan)
content:
Purpose: quick midquarter checkpoint to surface the strongest signals about my impact, blockers I want my manager to help remove, and micro-asks I will test over the next 6 weeks. This is a scratchpad — rough, prioritized, and intentionally actionable.

High-level framing (one-sentence): move hiring velocity and first-30-day activation in Customer Success by reducing friction in interview scheduling, scorecard alignment, and new-hire ramp curriculum.

Key signals I own / want to surface:
- Hiring velocity: offer-to-accept median for CS roles moved from 7 days to 4 days when we used dedicated recruiter block; need manager help to expand that template to 3 hiring squads.
- Time-to-hire (req open -> start): current median = 42 days; target = 30 days this quarter. Biggest contributor: loop between hiring manager feedback and scheduler availability (avg 8 days of wait).
- New hire activation: first-30-day activation metric (task completion + first-customer-touch) currently 62%; target 75%. Early signal: onboarding module completion rate falls off after week 1 (drop from 90% to 53%).

Concrete examples / evidence (short):
- Candidate X (CS-IC3): offered 2026-02-02, accepted 2026-02-04 after recruiter used two-day offer escrow. Correlates to - faster accept.
- Onboarding cohort Feb-2026 (n=6): average module completion day = 14; two engineers gave feedback that the 'product context' section is redundant with weekly kickoff (duplicate materials).
- Interviewer calibration sample (Jan 2026): 11/27 interviewers drifted on scorecard anchor question for 'customer empathy' (rating variance > 1.2).

Manager asks (specific, timeboxed):
1) Commit 2 hours this month to a short scorecard calibration workshop with hiring leads (objective: align on top-3 anchors and remove ambiguous rubrics). Outcome: updated scorecard doc + assigned owner per role.
2) Approve a 4-week experiment to reserve recruiter-blocks for 3 open CS reqs (cost-neutral if we reduce time-to-fill by 20%).
3) Introduce me to Engineering Product lead (Ana Ruiz) to sync onboarding curriculum overlap (15-min intro + shared doc).

My plan (next 6 weeks, micro-commitments):
- Week 1: run quick audit of open CS reqs and identify top 3 by impact; draft workshop agenda (2 hours).
- Week 2: pilot recruiter-block for one req; track offer cadence and candidate NPS touchpoint.
- Week 3: synthesize calibration notes, ship updated scorecard, and tag owners in Confluence.
- Week 4-6: run two onboarding micro-ups (trim redundant slides, add quick job-embedded tasks for week-1). Measure module completion and first-customer-touch.

Conversation prep — what I will say to manager (script bullets):
- Opening context: "Two short goals: speed up hiring by removing scheduling & calibration friction; and raise first-30-day activation by tightening week-1 learning tasks."
- Signal + impact: "We have examples where recruiter-blocks cut offer-to-accept by 3 days; with 3 squads this is a ~15% reduction in time-to-hire (est)."
- Asks (explicit): "Can you block 2 hours for the calibration session and greenlight a one-role recruiter-block pilot?"
- Friction to surface: "Scheduler capacity and inconsistent scorecard anchors are the two blockers I can't single-handedly change."

Example evidence snippets I will bring (short extracts):
- Slack clip: "@recruiting - candidate scheduling stalled for 6 days due to manager calendar gaps" (link).
- Candidate NPS: 'process was easy' — score 9/10 for those with recruiter-block; 6/10 otherwise.
- Confluence diff: onboarding-module v1 -> v1.2 shows 30% content redundant with 'team kickoff' doc.

Risks, unknowns, and quick mitigations:
- Risk: recruiter-blocks reduce short-term capacity for other reqs -> Mitigation: limit to highest impact reqs and set 2-week review.
- Unknown: how much of onboarding drop-off is caused by time-of-day scheduling vs content density -> Mitigation: run A/B for asynchronous micro-lessons vs full slide deck.
- Risk: calibration workshop attendance thin -> Mitigation: record session + produce 15-min digest for those who missed.

My success metrics (clear + measurable):
- Operational: time-to-hire median <= 30 days for prioritized CS reqs within 8 weeks.
- Quality: interviewer score variance on 'customer empathy' anchor reduced to <0.6.
- Activation: first-30-day activation >= 75% for the next cohort.

Quick backlog (things I might do if manager greenlights):
- Draft recruitment template for recruiter-blocks (scheduler windows, communication copy).
- Build a 1-page onboarding 'week-1 checklist' with job-embedded tasks.
- Create a short 'scorecard super-guide' for new interviewers (1 page + example answers).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Who is the canonical owner of the 'team kickoff' slide deck? I think Product Ops but need confirm. (Action: ask Ana Ruiz).
- Can we run recruiter-block as a cost-neutral swap for two low-priority reqs for 4 weeks? Need recruiter headcount owner input.
- Might be worth surfacing this at the People-ops all-hands if we have early positive signals.

Draft meeting agenda (30 minutes):
- 0-3 min: quick framing + 2 bullets of evidence.
- 3-12 min: propose experiments + ask for approvals.
- 12-22 min: discuss blockers and manager help.
- 22-28 min: assign owners + next steps.
- 28-30 min: quick recap and agree on check-in cadence.

Notes to self (tone & posture):
- Be concise: show 2 strong signals, one small request, and a clear next step.
- Bring evidence, not opinions.
- Avoid asking for broad resource increases — focus on targeted, reversible experiments.

Action items (today):
- Share this doc with Leila and Marcus for quick sanity check (done: pinged 2026-03-10).
- Draft agenda + send calendar invite for calibration week (target week-of 2026-03-22).
- Open Jira ticket: HR-NEWBATCH-2026 for pilot tracking.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after manager sync and after pilot week 2 results.

-- Riley
